Structural Causal Model

Structural causal model (SCM) for -data generation, and -for agent’s internal representation. Agent uses this model to prescribe treatment based on his prior beliefs before seeing new information, and based on his posterior beliefs after seeing new information.

Notes: Might be more efficient to reimplement the SCM class using pymc, especially as the Bayesian agent (agent model) is implemented using pymc.

A specific SCM with binary treatment A, continuous X and Y. This class inherits from SCM and sets the A_type to “binary”.

class scm.SCM(alpha_mu_X: float = 80, alpha_sigma_X: float = 10, alpha_mu_A: float = 2, alpha_sigma_A: float = 1.0, alpha_mu_Y: float = 0.0, alpha_sigma_Y: float = 0.1, N_E: float = 1.0, a: float = 12.0, b: float = -0.1, d: float = 0.125)[source]

Bases: object

Class for SCM with continuous A, continuous X, and continuous Y. This SCM encodes information so that

N_Xi ~ N(alpha_mu_X, alpha_sigma_X)

N_Yi ~ N(alpha_mu_Y, alpha_sigma_Y)

N_Ai ~ N(alpha_mu_A, alpha_sigma_A)

Y_i = a + b * X_i + N_E * A_i + N_Yi

A_i = d * X_i + N_Ai

X_i = N_Xi

Parameters:

  • alpha_mu_X (float) – Mean of X

  • alpha_sigma_X (float) – Standard deviation of X

  • alpha_mu_A (float) – Mean of A

  • alpha_sigma_A (float) – Standard deviation of A

  • alpha_mu_Y (float) – Mean of Y

  • alpha_sigma_Y (float) – Standard deviation of Y

  • N_E (float) – Effect size. The effect size is a fixed number. All variability is explained by variance in other RVs.

  • a (float) – Constant for SCM

  • b (float) – Constant for SCM

  • d (float) – Constant for SCM

N_E: float = 1.0
a: float = 12.0
alpha_mu_A: float = 2

alpha_sigma_X: float = 10

get_CATE_mu(A1_treatment, A0_treatment)[source]

This method returns the mean of the CATE-distribution given X, A1_treatment, and A0_treatment. Due to how the SCM is defined, this value is equivalent to (A1_treatment - A0_treatment) * self.N_E.

The SCM in this class is defined so that Y given A and X is normally distributed and its parameters are deterministically determined by the values of A and X. This results in the CATE- distibution also being normal and allows for deterministic calculation of the mean as:

CATE_mu(X) = E(Y| X, do(A=A1)) - E(Y| X, do(A=A0))

Parameters:

  • A1_treatment (float) – Dosage value of higher dose treatment

  • A0_treatment (float) – Dosage value of lower dose treatment

sample(X=None, A=None, draws=1, rng=None)[source]

This method encodes the structure of the SCM and generates samples of X, Y, and A:

\(X, A, Y \sim p(X, Y, A)\)

If X is passed, then the output A and Y are conditional on the value of X:

\(A, Y \sim p(A, Y| X)\)

If A is passed, the output Y is conditional on the intervention do(A):

\(X, Y \sim p(X, Y| do(A))\)

If both X and Y are passed, the output is conditional on X and on the intervention do(A):

\(Y \sim p(Y| X, do(A))\)

All of X, A, and Y are always returned. In addition, the distribution parameters for Y (mu_Y_cond, and std_Y_cond) are returned. If X and/or A are provided, the distribution parameters are conditional on the given values. Otherwise they are “conditional” only on the sampled values (in contrast how the word “conditional” is normally used).

Parameters:

  • X – Optional input. If provided, output will be conditional on X.

  • A – Optional input. If provided, output will be conditional on do(A).

  • draws (int) – Size of sample to generate.

  • rng – seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility

This method samples the CATE-distribution using treatment 1 (higher dosage) instead of treatment 0. Given X and two treatment options A1_treatment and A0_treatment

Parameters:

  • X (float) – Feature to condition on

  • A1_treatment (float) – Dosage value of higher dose treatment

  • A0_treatment (float) – Dosage value of lower dose treatment

  • draws (int) – Size of sample to generate

  • rng – seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility

sample_do_A(A_treatment, X: ndarray, draws: int = 1, rng=None) → ndarray[source]

Generates sample from the SCM given the data and set treatments, i.e.

Y_i ~ p(Y|do(A_treatment), X)

Returns an array with shape (n, *X.shape). This is merely a wrapper for the interventional path in self.sample().

Parameters:

  • A_treatment (int- or array-like) – value to intervene on A, or array with X.shape

  • X – observed values of X

  • draws (int) – Size of sample to draw for every observation in A.

  • rng – seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility
